anomalies.observed: The 5 V buck feedback divider is drawn as R55 = 68k (top, to +5V) and R5 = 19k6 (bottom, to GND), with the FB pin (REG2.23) at their junction. With the MIC26903 0.8 V reference this gives Vout = 0.8*(1+68k/19.6k) = 3.58 V, not 5 V.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the 5 V rail is set by Vout = 0.8*(1+R5/R6); for a 5 V output the divider ratio must be Rtop/Rbot = 5.25 (e.g. 68k/13k or 100k/19k), so the drawn 68k/19k6 divider is inconsistent with a 5 V rail.

evidence.quote: R55 68k ... R5 19k6 ... Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6) (Power sheet, REG2 MIC26903YJL-TR feedback network)
5 V rail: A MIC26903YJL-TR synchronous buck regulator steps the battery input down to 5 V. Design notes on this section: ... feedback divider relation Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)

anomalies.impact: The 5 V rail would regulate to about 3.6 V instead of 5 V, starving the servo/PWM bank, GPS module and USB-UART bridges and causing the 3.3 V LDO input to be out of specification.

parsed.summary: The power sheet's 5 V buck feedback divider (R55=68k / R5=19k6) computes to ~3.6 V rather than the specified 5 V, which is the only clear deviation found; the rest of the drawn design (including the documented barometer RESET/EOC mix-up) matches the specification.
